note: Attacker-controlled bytes are copied into a mutable buffer and passed to the config parser as the fuzzing input.
The fuzz input becomes the backing storage for the configuration lexer/parser without additional validation.
A linefeed after buffered strings selects the shorthand section path, which is the vulnerable control-flow edge.
The shorthand handler delegates to parse_section and then emits an extra SECTION_END marker if parsing succeeds.
The first buffered string token is consumed as the section name, and subsequent buffered strings are appended into the shared strbuf.
Each attacker-controlled token length is appended into the dynamic string buffer, growing it as needed.

The sink copies sz bytes from the attacker-controlled lexeme into the destination buffer; the crash is a global-buffer-overflow read when sz exceeds the available source bytes for the malformed token layout.
